target_customer: Small businesses that need a phone system with extensions, forwarding and voicemail without IT setup
problem: Small businesses wanted a business phone system as easy as Google Voice, without PBX hardware or IT staff.
business_model: SaaS subscription with tiers at $10, $24 and $70 per month

founders.name: Jason Corwin
founders.background_notes: From the YC page bio; later co-founder of Safely Finance (YC S19).

founders.name: Conor Lee
previous_startups: Hiplead (bootstrapped to $8M ARR per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Named with Corwin in TechCrunch 2011 launch coverage.

founders.name: Zain Memon
founders.background_notes: Listed by YC as co-founder; TechCrunch 2011 names only Corwin and Lee. The YC bio mixes later roles (Opendoor, Eureka, Synapticure), so only Movity is treated as clearly earlier.

exit.reason: Not public; YC lists the company as inactive.

competitors.name: Grasshopper
competitors.what: Virtual business phone system for small businesses

competitors.name: Google Voice
competitors.what: Free consumer phone number, forwarding and voicemail transcription; TellFi positioned as the paid business version

technical_complexity.rationale: Built on existing telephony carriers with extensions, forwarding and transcription; TellFi said it was not VoIP, relying on regular lines.

defensibility.rationale: Features were essentially the same across three price tiers and Grasshopper offered similar service.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says what incumbents did in response.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2011-02-28) reported over 50 clients at launch, and ReadWrite reported heavy demand from Canadian users prompting a free one-year Canadian offer.

branding.domain_note: Used tellfi.com (exact .com); it now redirects to a domain-sale page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned on simplicity with no IT setup, per TechCrunch

brand_strength.rationale: Only launch coverage found; searches for brand material surfaced unrelated companies with similar names.

outcome_analysis: TellFi launched in February 2011 as Google Voice for business, with over 50 clients at launch and paid plans from $10 a month. YC lists it as inactive; no funding, acquisition, shutdown notice or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: No funding information found beyond YC backing (several searches returned only unrelated companies such as TellApart and telli). The YC page lists three founders while TechCrunch names two. tellfi.com redirect to a domain-sale page was observed from the redirect header, not fetched.
